clusters.name: Cluster B: Persistent Grief Response
items: Intense yearning/longing for the deceased person (DSM p.322)
Preoccupation with thoughts or memories of the deceased (in children/adolescents, preoccupation may focus on circumstances of death) (DSM p.323)

clusters.name: Cluster C: Cognitive, Emotional, Behavioral Distress
items: Identity disruption (feeling as though part of oneself has died) (DSM p.323)
Marked sense of disbelief about the death (DSM p.323)
Avoidance of reminders that the person is dead (DSM p.323)
Intense emotional pain (anger, bitterness, sorrow) related to death (DSM p.323)
Difficulty reintegrating into relationships and activities (DSM p.323)
Feeling that life is meaningless (DSM p.323)
Intense loneliness as a result of death (DSM p.323)

criteria.thresholds: Death >=12 months ago in adults, >=6 months ago in children/adolescents; >=1 Cluster B symptom and >=3 Cluster C symptoms present most days, nearly every day for past month (DSM p.322-323)
subtypes: With traumatic bereavement (homicide or suicide) (Dulcan p.350, p.352)

epidemiology.prevalence: ~9.8% in bereaved adults globally (DSM p.324); ~18% PCBD among bereaved US youth in community (DSM p.324, Dulcan p.349)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Higher prevalence/severity reported in females (DSM p.325, Dulcan p.351)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Can occur at any age after loss; higher risk in older adults and parents after death of a child (DSM p.324)
epidemiology.prognosis: Chronic course if untreated; elevated risk for cardiovascular disease, hypertension, suicidal ideation, and long-term academic/developmental impairment in youth (DSM p.326, Dulcan p.352)

items: Normal Grief: Affect is waves of emptiness/loss (pangs of grief) with preserved self-esteem and capacity for humor (DSM p.176, p.326)
Major Depressive Disorder (MDD): Persistent depressed mood, pervasive anhedonia, worthlessness, self-loathing; bereavement exclusion removed in DSM-5-TR (DSM p.184, p.327; Dulcan p.246)
PTSD: Intrusions focus on traumatic event/threat rather than relationship; avoidance of trauma triggers rather than loss reminders; yearning is absent in PTSD (DSM p.327; Dulcan p.355)
Separation Anxiety Disorder: Distress focuses on fear of separation from living attachment figures, not deceased person (DSM p.221, p.327)
key_numbers: 6 months: Minimum duration required for children/adolescents for PGD diagnosis (DSM p.322)
12 months: Minimum duration required for adults for PGD diagnosis (DSM p.322)
3 of 8: Minimum Criterion C symptoms required for diagnosis (DSM p.323)

items: 3 core components of death concept: Finality/Irreversibility, Universality, Causality/Non-functionality (Dulcan p.55, p.349)
Preschoolers (<5 years): Magical thinking, searching for deceased, play themes of physical reunion (ladder to heaven), somatic complaints, developmental regression (DSM p.325; Dulcan p.352-354)
School-age (6-11 years): Self-blame, fear for remaining caregivers, identity disruption ('feeling different' during Mother's Day cards), academic decline (DSM p.325; Dulcan p.354)
Adolescents (12-18 years): Emotional numbness, reckless behavior, feeling 'robbed' of developmental guidance, substance use, suicidal ideation (DSM p.325; Dulcan p.352)
Traumatic Bereavement: Severe PTSD intrusive symptoms block ability to access positive, comforting memories of deceased (Dulcan p.351, p.357)
key_numbers: 3: Core cognitive components of death concept (Finality, Universality, Causality) (Dulcan p.55, p.349)
6 months: Pediatric PGD duration threshold (DSM p.322)

first_line: TF-CBT with Grief Modules (PRACTICE + grief psychoeducation, resolving ambivalence, preserving positive memories, converting relationship from interaction to memory) (Dulcan p.357-358)
CBITS (Cognitive-Behavioral Intervention for Trauma in Schools) - group format in schools (Dulcan p.358)
TGCT-A (Trauma Grief Component Therapy for Adolescents) - 5 sequential modules (Dulcan p.358)
Child-Parent Psychotherapy (CPP) - dyadic therapy for ages 0-6 (Dulcan p.358)
IPT-A (Interpersonal Psychotherapy for Adolescents) - Grief problem area (Dulcan p.958, p.961)
second_line: Pharmacotherapy is NOT first-line for PGD alone; used only for comorbid MDD/PTSD or severe dysfunction (Dulcan p.356, p.361)
Fluoxetine (FDA-approved for pediatric depression from age 8) (StahlKids p.208; Dulcan p.260)
key_side_effects: Treatment-Emergent Activation Syndrome (TEAS) from SSRIs: motor restlessness, impulsivity, insomnia (StahlKids p.93, p.185; Dulcan p.260)
FDA Black Box Warning for suicidal ideation/behavior with SSRIs in youth (4% vs 2% placebo) (StahlKids p.92; Dulcan p.260)
treatment.monitoring: Weekly face-to-face monitoring for TEAS and suicidality during initial 4 weeks of SSRI treatment (StahlKids p.93; Dulcan p.261)

high_yield: PGD duration criterion is >=6 months for children/adolescents vs >=12 months for adults (DSM p.322).
DSM-5-TR removed Bereavement Exclusion for MDD; bereavement is recognized as a severe stressor triggering MDE (DSM p.184; Dulcan p.246).
In grief, affect comes in waves of emptiness/loss with preserved self-esteem; in MDD, mood is persistently depressed with self-loathing and anhedonia (DSM p.176; Dulcan p.247).
Traumatic bereavement occurs when death is violent or accidental; PTSD symptoms interfere with processing grief (Dulcan p.351).
Grief Modules in TF-CBT emphasize converting the relationship with the deceased from interaction to memory (Dulcan p.351, p.358).
No primary pharmacotherapy for PGD alone; psychotherapies (TF-CBT, CBITS, CPP, IPT-A) are first-line (Dulcan p.356-358, p.361).
Fluoxetine is the only FDA-approved SSRI for depression in children under 12 (from age 8) (StahlKids p.208; Dulcan p.260).
